usageNotes: Use this to check the live runtime state of a specific PVE-managed system service on a given node — useful for health checks, troubleshooting, or pre-flight validation before restarting or reconfiguring a service. The node must be online and reachable; requires Sys.Audit on /nodes/{node}. Returns three distinct systemd state dimensions (active-state, state/SubState, unit-state) which together give a full picture: a service can be enabled (unit-state) but not currently running (active-state=inactive).

examples.summary: Check whether pveproxy is running on node pve1

tips: active-state is the high-level systemd ActiveState (e.g. 'active', 'failed'); state is the finer-grained SubState (e.g. 'running', 'dead') — check both when diagnosing failures.
unit-state reflects whether the service is enabled to start at boot ('enabled'), disabled, or masked — a service can be running but 'disabled' if it was started manually.
Poll this endpoint after issuing a service restart (post_nodes_node_services_service_restart) to confirm the state transitions from 'activating' to 'active'.
The 'corosync' and 'pve-cluster' services are cluster-critical — if either shows active-state='failed', expect degraded quorum or HA instability across all nodes.
